newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-LAZIO SIGN JUGOVIC FROM JUVENTUS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LAZIO SIGN JUGOVIC FROM JUVENTUS.

text.p: Lazio presented new signing Vladimir Jugovic on Tuesday with the Yugoslav midfielder saying he was still stunned to be leaving Juventus.
"I am a bit stunned by this move," Jugovic said of his move from Turin.
"Evidently Juventus decided to rejuvenate. Juventus decided first, I know that (coach Marcello) Lippi would have liked to keep me."

Club sources said Jugovic, the latest big name departure from Juve after Gianluca Vialli, Fabrizio Ravanelli and Paulo Sousa at the end of 1995-96, had signed a four-year contract with the Rome club worth around $1.2 million a season.
The player, who helped Juventus win the league last season and the European Cup the year before, is expected to be joined later by Croat former club mate Alen Boksic.
Boksic has yet to sign for Lazio, his former club before moving to Juventus, although the move is considered little more than a formality in Italy.

Lazio will be run by Sampdoria's former boss Sven-Goran Eriksson next season, a Swedish coach who worked with Jugovic in Genoa before the Yugoslav moved to Juventus and who has also signed Sampdoria striker Roberto Mancini.
"Eriksson, a coach I know well, was the most important part of my decision," said Jugovic.
